verdict.rationale: 2FAS Auth documents syncing tokens through the user's own iCloud or Google Drive. However, this is framed mainly as protection against phone loss, and nothing confirms that tokens stay live on a phone and a tablet at the same time. On the computer, the browser extension pairs with the phone and each code must be confirmed in the mobile app, so tokens are not independently synced to the desktop. The "Multi-device sync" listing appears to belong to the paid tier of 2FAS Pass, the password manager, not to the Auth tokens. Missing for 10: documented automatic simultaneous multi-device token sync (phone and tablet), standalone token access on the computer without the phone, cross-platform (iOS/Android) sync, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an everyday user, my tokens are available on my phone, tablet, and computer at the same time, kept in sync automatically

citations.quote: Synchronize your Tokens with 2FAS export files, iCloud or Google Drive.
You can enable secure data syncing with your personal iCloud or Google Drive to protect yourself from losing Tokens in case of phone damage or loss.
The 2FAS Auth browser extension pairs with your phone to deliver 2FA tokens where you sign in
